Problem 124. Pairwise collective choice: Library versus Park
Group preferences can be aggregated in different ways. Pairwise majority asks a specific question about two options at a time.

Three public projects are considered: Park, Library, Sports Hall. Voter groups and rankings: 7 voters rank Park>Library>Sports Hall; 4 voters rank Library>Sports Hall>Park; 5 voters rank Sports Hall>Park>Library. Use pairwise majority: compare two options at a time; each voter supports the one ranked higher.
For a pairwise contest, count how many voters prefer each of the two options. Ignore the third option for that comparison.
In a pairwise vote between Library and Park, which option wins?
1. For each group, check whether Library or Park is ranked higher. 2. Totals: Library=4, Park=12. 3. Therefore the result is Park.

Part B — New and mixed reasoning domains
Map scale links a model to the real world through proportional reasoning.
A map has scale 1:10000. The measured map distance between two points is 3 cm. Rule: 1 cm on the map represents 10000 cm in reality; 100,000 cm = 1 km.
Multiply map length by the scale denominator, then convert units. A scale is a ratio, not an added distance.
What is the real straight-line distance in kilometres?
Scale problems are ratio problems: keep units explicit and conversion becomes mechanical.
Proportion d_real=d_map×denominator, followed by unit conversion.
